language.howToChooseYourGradeIntro: Our curriculum Grades K to 6 corresponds with ages:
language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hi, I'm Chip.
Hello, my name is Kylie. This is my dad’s store and I like to come in sometimes and help him wait on the customers and take inventory.
You can help too! Summer is almost here and it is our busiest season!
Perhaps you can help us behind the counter. This time of year the cash register is always busy. Oh, and by the way, the currency around here is clamshells.
We also sell some summer toys. These colorful beach balls sell so fast, we can hardly keep the basket stocked.
Each time we sell the balls, we have to count how much a customer has to pay. One beach ball costs 6 clamshells. This means two balls cost 2 x 6 = 12 clamshells.
We also need your help with taking inventory to discover how many articles we need to have in the store.
Sometimes customers want to purchase more than one item, like beach balls and hats. For example, 3 kids may come to the store looking for 2 beach balls each.
So, the kids are buying 6 beach balls in total. Do you remember how to multiply by 3s and 6s? Let's practice counting by 3s now!
and so on…. And how about 6s?
By multiplying a number by 3 you get multiples of 3, and by multiplying the number by 6 you get multiples of 6.
Do you remember how to multiply by 3s and by 6s? Let's practice counting by 3s right now!
